newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends firm as Europe freeze lifts gas oil.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends firm as Europe freeze lifts gas oil.

text.p: IPE Brent crude ended firm on Monday after a session dominated by weather-inspired gains in the gas oil contract, but weaker U.S. markets drew some of the rally's sting, brokers said.
A severe cold snap throughout Europe encouraged demand, particularly for gas oil (heating oil) from Germany, the continent's single largest market.
But relatively mild weather in the key U.S. northeast kept U.S. gains to a minimum and capped London's rally.
Feb Brent crude added 26 cents to close at $23.68 a barrel while NYMEX crude gained just 13 cents.
Feb Brent touched a high of $23.97 a barrel in early trade before light profit-taking shortly after NYMEX dealing began pulled the contract to its session low of $23.55.
"It was clearly a tale of two markets today," said a broker.
"There was a lack of follow-through buying on NYMEX and you can't blame them - it may be cold here but it's relatively warm over there," he added.
Jan gas oil closed at its session high of $223.00 a tonne, up $6.00 from Friday and pulling the prompt intermonth spread out $3.50 to a $5.00 backwardation by the close.

Forecasters said the icy conditions, which have claimed at least 90 lives and brought snow as far south as the Mediterranean island of Corsica, may continue until late this week, with further heavy snowfalls and sub-normal temperatures possible.
